units.text: Negotiators were authorized $10 million for New Orleans and the Floridas.

citations.title:
37 reactions | 4 cents an acre. 530 million acres. A deal that changed everything — for better and for worse.

In 1803, negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe went to France authorized to spend $10 million on the port of New Orleans. They came back having agreed to pay $15 million for an area larger than Great Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Portugal combined.

The Louisiana Purchase doubled the size of the United States — and set in motion the forced displacement of thousands of American Indians across dozens of tribes who had long called this land home.

The original documents are on display now as part of The Story of US: America 250 exhibit at the Truman Library. Tap the link in bio to plan your visit.
